# CI2 native hosted carrier

This is preparation for a new measured `native-hosted-v1` qualification. It does not establish native CI2 PASS or authorize a qualification run. The profile admits one exact eleven-field Docker/init identity tuple separately reviewed from public observation run `35284410573`; every future qualification must reproduce the complete tuple and pass fresh capacity, device, daemon, source, image, owner-entry and exact-head event gates. Native init adoption, strict Linux process cleanup, hosted cancellation fixtures, the historical four Minors and CV13 remain open.

The carrier runs on a fresh public GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` x64 VM. Product source remains commit `ab9ec0a1c27e257f7d96be1e3011f6e5f274a609`, tree `3219ed991de31ada4e20ebd720aa192b15c04ca6`, base `50f0a6d9f95aa50e7b19af7efbb836a1b16b9c6f`; neither the PR merge ref nor carrier HEAD is product source. A fresh complete-history bundle is generated once, verified through an isolated clone, and bound by its new size/hash in `prepared.json`. The historical packing hash in the profile is provenance, not the new bundle acceptance hash. Source/carrier preparations never mount credentials, host home, cache, or Docker socket into the workload.

Exactly nine historical runtime files are copied byte for byte. `ci2-runtime-v16.sha256` is a **new native 13-entry manifest**; its retained basename serves the unchanged transfer helper. The historical manifest digest is `d5c0a01bc0286cdf044e13eca40843ca9fae0562ea61d9b7a3f7792f44853036`. The workflow pins the separate profile and native manifest digests, while the profile avoids a self-referential new-manifest hash. Bootstrap, worker, container runner and toolchain verifier are the four explicitly reviewed runtime derivatives. Product source, targets and configuration flags remain unchanged; this correction changes toolchain evidence and its descriptive provenance policy.

Carrier checkout has a separate, finite bootstrap. It downloads only the two existing watchdog/diagnostic helpers from fixed paths at the exact event head on `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/housegate/housegate/`, verifies their predeclared SHA256 hashes, and then executes those existing owners. Initial reads have a 3-second socket timeout, a 20-second total deadline and a 64 KiB per-helper cap; redirects, proxies, credentials, existing destinations and noncanonical repository/head identities are refused. The control file is private/exclusive and limited to 32 KiB. Under the verified owner, the pinned 13-entry manifest (4 KiB), remaining helpers (1 MiB each) and profile (64 KiB) are downloaded with the same origin/hash rules and a 16 MiB aggregate bootstrap bound. Failure before child ownership exists produces only a bounded console refusal; after ownership, command stdout/stderr/status and staging receipts are retained locally. Checkout failure cannot start source/image preparation.

The existing owner then supervises depth-one, blob-filtered, sparse Git fetch/checkout of the native carrier directory and this workflow. Checkout receives at most 90 seconds within the original 300-second preparation envelope, leaving the unspent balance for source/image admission. The command adapter measures combined staging before, during and after each Git command. Git head/tree, clean state, manifest/profile and run/attempt bind the checkout receipt; `admission.json` additionally binds the workflow hash. This shallow carrier history does not relax the separate complete frozen product-history/bundle verification.

## Exact event protocol

Initial `opened`, `synchronize` and `reopened` events run preparation checks only. After independent exact-head review, root may add `ci2-env-<full40hexhead>` for a bounded **read-only observation**. Only that exact `labeled` event is admitted. Observation reads the fixed local Docker endpoint, fixed host files, and version outputs; it never pulls, creates, starts or execs a container, installs a package or changes daemon state. The bounded observation artifact contains a candidate identity tuple and measured capacity; root must separately review and commit any admitted tuple/profile revision. Run `35284410573` supplied the currently admitted candidate through that review path. Future observed values never populate the allowlist automatically.

Qualification requires its own exact `labeled` event `ci2-ok-<full40hexhead>`, same `housegate/housegate` base/head repository, exact `urwt/codex/issue-153-ci2-native` branch, non-draft PR, `run_attempt == 1`, reviewed profile/manifest/source binding, nonempty tuple allowlist, fresh capacity admission and one local immutable attempt lease. An observation label never authorizes qualification. An old label remaining in the PR label list, unrelated label, changed head, reopened event or workflow rerun is insufficient. Root owns the external one-attempt record and must not remove/reapply a label as a retry; there is no remote state store or token write. There is no `workflow_dispatch` or default-branch dependency.

## New measured resource contract

| Item | Native hosted contract |
| --- | --- |
| Native platform | Linux x86_64 host, Linux x86_64/amd64 daemon, Linux/amd64 image; finite admitted runner/Docker/cgroup/init tuple |
| CPU | At least 4 host/daemon CPUs; 3 workload CPUs |
| Memory | Host/daemon total at least 15,000,000,000 bytes; available at least 13,958,643,712 bytes immediately before create; workload memory and memory-swap both 12 GiB |
| PIDs/init | 1024; explicit `--init`, observed `HostConfig.Init=true`, injected PID1 executable hash and effective cgroup v2 limits |
| Tmpfs | `/ci2` exec 6 GiB; `/tmp` noexec 128 MiB; shm 64 MiB, charged within workload memory |
| Disk | At least 10 GiB before pull and 8 GiB before create; same-device paths are recorded together rather than counted as independent reserves |
| Monitored disk budgets | Image allocation/transient unpack 3 GiB; source/carrier 512 MiB; layer 512 MiB; Docker logs 40 MiB; host evidence 512 MiB; archive 1 GiB; other scratch 1 GiB |
| Evidence/cache | Container evidence 500 MiB; host evidence 512 MiB with 2 MiB tail reserve; disk cache disabled; no active GC target (profile value 0) |

The `tmpfs-single-output-v1` policy keeps the same `/ci2/cache/output-root`, workspace and Bazel server, forces `--disk_cache=`, and removes the inactive disk-cache GC flag. `/ci2/cache/disk` remains an empty disabled-cache sentinel under the existing account/mode boundary; unexpected content refuses without deletion. Both cache receipts identify `disk_cache=disabled`, `disk_cache_flag=--disk_cache=`, `disk_cache_gc_max_size=not-applicable` and the separate sentinel path. Existing phase/final usage samples add only fixed output-root/sentinel/XDG/tmp rows. These are sampled observations, not continuous peaks; nested parent/child rows must not be summed. No new monitor, mount, cache cleanup or retry is introduced.

Actual run `35293495164` remains a spent, sealed FAIL with observed strict ordinary-failure cleanup: GoLink reported ENOSPC, and the final 6 GiB tmpfs sample was 97%. It does not quantify bytes saved by disabling the second cache or prove that 6 GiB will suffice. The unchanged hard limit still fails closed. Later CI-test/FFI/release phases, controlled native init adoption and hosted cancellation remain unexecuted; original historical findings and CV13 stay open. This source candidate requires fresh exact-head review and separate one-shot admission before another run.

Phase-observed layer/image/cache bounds are acceptance checks, not hard kernel quotas. No pruning, host package installation, quota reconfiguration, resource escalation, host compiler fallback or automatic clean/retry is permitted. The unchanged six phases retain setup300/Homebrew300/CI-build540/CI-tests-and-FFI840/Linux-release420/Darwin-release420 clocks, exact commands, private pipes, actual joins and one host-selected finalizer. The invalid CC remains `/ci2/forbidden-host-cc`; Homebrew still proves no Zig selection, and CI/Linux/Darwin retain their explicit Zig selections. The CI test phase fetches frozen v0.10.0 FFI and runs the existing full non-manual CI test surface; it does not prove separately listed Docker integration targets ran.

The single 512 MiB staging inventory charges `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (including `.git`), the owned `input` directory (including bootstrap downloads, source history, bundle and verification clone), and `execution/runtime` together. Canonical root aliases/overlap are inode-deduplicated; distinct files on a shared device still count separately. Child symlinks are charged without following them, and hardlinks are refused. Other execution evidence is excluded from this staging sum and retains its separate evidence cap. Runtime copies are checked before and after each file. Each owned command records before/peak/after measurements, actual over-budget observations, exit and reap; the 50 ms sampling interval can permit transient overshoot, so this is monitored acceptance, not a kernel quota. An observed excess terminates the existing owner and refuses further work. After source preparation, the actual pre-pull boundary freshly checks root, carrier and Docker backing-device identity and at least 10 GiB free on each; the later pre-create 8 GiB check is separate.

## Clocks and cancellation

The 65-minute job accounts for 300 seconds checkout/preparation, 3300 seconds owner (3060 work plus 240 cleanup), 180 seconds archive/upload and 120 seconds transitions. Preparation shares one clock across checkout and adapter work. The qualification step is 56 minutes. Existing shutdown20/22/24, termination20/5/30, stop10, remote50/80 and host60/90 transport budgets remain unchanged. Early failure cleanup is bounded by the earlier original deadline or failure+240, preserving the final 60-second teardown reserve.

The explicit owner admission boundary is the short `owner-entry` step, whose condition evaluates `!cancelled()`. It emits a timestamped entry grant; bootstrap refuses a missing grant or one older than 15 seconds. Cancellation known before that step refuses the owner. Cancellation after that grant may allow the original bounded owner to start/finish under `always()`, including the at-most-15-second grant-to-bootstrap window. This is an explicit pending cancellation contract, not an assertion that `job.status` is equivalent to `cancelled()`. The running qualification step never reevaluates `!cancelled()` as its own cancellation condition. Root must review this boundary and obtain the separately authorized live GitHub cancellation fixture before depending on it. Forced cancellation, runner disappearance and hard timeout may kill it; these remain unsealed with cleanup unproved unless terminal receipts survived. VM disposal does not prove strict observed server/container absence. No detached daemon or second finalizer is introduced. The separately gated `--native-fixture init_adoption` and `--native-fixture github_cancellation` entries explicitly refuse without future fixture authority; their tests do not substitute local simulation for native evidence.

## Receipts and independent acceptance

`admission.json` binds PR head/ref, repository, event merge SHA, PR, run/attempt, carrier tree, workflow hash, runtime-manifest hash and profile hash. `observation.json` records host/daemon/socket/init identity, capacity and filesystem devices/free bytes. `prepared.json` adds source raw commit objects/hashes, five-file delta hashes, new bundle packing identity and preparation time. `attempt-lease.json` consumes the run's workload attempt before the owner starts. Every capture retains bounded stdout/stderr/status; interrupted captures remain started/unsealed. No successful container evidence manifest is rewritten.

An image-configuration refusal keeps the same exact image ID, pinned RepoDigest and six-field tuple comparisons. Its existing `export/refusal.json` additionally retains bounded `actual` and profile-derived `expected` values for `os`, `architecture`, `size`, `user`, `entrypoint` and `workdir`, a fixed-name `mismatch_names` list, and booleans confirming that the preceding ID and RepoDigest checks passed. Each UTF-8 string is limited to 512 bytes, each list to 16 strings, image size to a non-negative signed 64-bit integer, and the complete refusal to 16 KiB. Missing, malformed or oversized inspect data still refuses without exporting partial image details; unrelated preparation failures retain the generic refusal schema. The raw inspect object, image environment and unsealed command directory are never transported by this path.

After fresh `host-admit` image comparison, the worker consumes the compact `id|os|architecture|size|user|entrypoint|workdir` summary from that same adapter. It derives every field from the exact-digest profile bound to `prepared.admission.profile_sha256`, with existing image field limits, compact JSON entrypoint and a bounded delimiter-safe summary. `native-admission.json` records that profile digest and summary before it reaches preflight; no second static tuple is maintained. Old sealed preflight receipts remain unchanged.

Hosted qualification [run 35291077452](https://github.com/housegate/housegate/actions/runs/35291077452) directly observed image size `1065590879`: the exact image ID and RepoDigest membership passed, and `os`, `architecture`, `user`, `entrypoint` and `workdir` matched the profile. The profile now pins that exact size. The run refused before owner or workload startup and provides no runtime acceptance.

After the exact owned container is retired, `container-absence.json` records successful exact-ID and exact-name empty listings against the admitted endpoint. `owner-return.json` records the outer watchdog's return; a timeout/orphan/signal result cannot prove cleanup. Only after those records, complete host command boundaries and received container seal does archival write `terminal.json` and `HOST-MANIFEST.sha256`. Unsealed cases retain bounded diagnostics and truthful terminal fields. `ci2-native.tar` contains only execution files plus four named input receipts, including hidden owner files. The sidecar `archive.json` binds its checksum, byte count, inventory, run/head/profile and terminal outcome. Upload uses a unique run/attempt/head name, no overwrite, missing-file error, and 14-day retention. GitHub artifact digest is an additional transport layer.

Root must download the exact artifact, verify the outer checksum and bounded path/type/count inventory, all host/container manifests, source/carrier/profile/image/run binding and raw terminal predicates. A green job or successful upload does not independently establish CI2 PASS.

| Outcome | Acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| All six phases, strict shutdown/server absence, actual joins, seals, transfer, exact container absence and downloaded artifact verified | Exact native-profile CI2 PASS only, after independent review |
| Original phase failure retained, single fail finalizer and strict cleanup/seals verified | Sealed FAIL; attempt consumed |
| Lost identity, incomplete handoff, truncation, timeout, forced cancellation or missing seal/absence/join | Unsealed FAIL or cleanup-unproved; never PASS |
| Empty tuple/low capacity/drift/cancellation before create | Admission refused; no workload result |

## Exact-owned cleanup boundary

The worker alone retires its full 64-hex container ID after matching exact name, task, run, frozen commit and owner labels and rechecking the fixed endpoint. It retains stop10 and bounded remove operations, then separately proves exact-ID and exact-name absence. A lost daemon/ownership identity refuses destructive cleanup. There is no glob/name-prefix cleanup, daemon prune or host-tree cleanup. If an owner is forcibly lost, root must inspect the saved full ID and endpoint/labels and separately authorize any remaining cleanup; VM disappearance is not a cleanup receipt.

Run `python3 -B .github/ci2/native-v1/test-native-carrier.py` for finite parser, serialization, clock, source-Git, resource, image, init-field and archive cases. Native init adoption, process/cgroup behavior and hosted cancellation require separately authorized future native fixture evidence. The finite source fixtures also execute the private wrapper with an argv-only stub, reject storage-policy drift and disabled-sentinel contents, and exercise the image-summary admission branch with bounded local data; they do not execute the native workload. Reviewers should compare all four runtime derivatives against the pinned historical bytes and independently recheck the new manifest/profile identities before any label operation.

R145 adds a source-backed `rules_go_0_62_cgo_compilepkg` compiler proof alongside direct `CppCompile`. CI requires the exact local Linux platform; release mode flags and platforms stay separate. Only cquery gains `--consistent_labels`. The verifier requires configured reachability, direct C provider edges, owned executable hashes/action inputs, a pinned active secp256k1 cgo source, and the supported builder generation chain. Root GoLink records configured extld provenance, without asserting that an external-linker child executed.

The collector retains an explicit bounded source set (128 KiB per file, 1 MiB total; 2 MiB serialized receipt) inside the ordinary evidence manifest and existing phase/stream/global limits. Local source pins are expected authority; future owned bytes must independently match. No source walk, compiler execution or extra runtime authority is introduced by collection. `test-toolchain-evidence.py` uses synthetic owned executable files that are hashed but never executed; fixture evidence cannot qualify a native attempt. Run 35299151107 and all earlier sealed failures remain spent failures. Native tests, FFI, releases and fault gates remain open.
